newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan parliament rejects bid to reshuffle cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan parliament rejects bid to reshuffle cabinet.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party blocked an attempt by opposition lawmakers on Friday to put forward a motion asking President Lee Teng-hui to replace Premier Lien Chan and order a full cabinet reshuffle.
"The (opposition's) motion was voted not to be raised during today's parliament session," a parliamentary spokesman said.

Parliament rejected a proposal to discuss the opposition's motion by a vote of 74 to 63. The vote came after three cabinet-level ministers resigned on Thursday, increasing pressure on the government ahead of a planned cabinet reshuffle triggered by public discontent over rising crime.
Minister without portfolio Ma Ying-jeou, Interior Minister Lin Feng-cheng and agriculture council chairman Tjiu Mau-ying decided to resign.
Premier Lien also tendered his resignation earlier in the week. Lee declined to accept, but asked Lien to propose changes in cabinet positions next week.
Anti-government sentiment erupted after police discovered the naked body of 17-year-old Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping, floating in a river last week.
Police said Pai Hsiao-yen had been kidnapped and murdered. Her killers remain at large.
More than 50,000 people marched in Taipei on Sunday to protest against Pai's murder and demand the resignation of Lien and a cabinet reshuffle.
But the cabinet's Government Information Office on Friday released crime statistics that it said showed "the overall state of social order in Taiwan remains stable".
The office, quoting data from the National Police Administration, said Taipei convicted a total of 130,133 criminals in 1996, down 13.9 percent from 1993.
The data also showed the number of violent crime cases on the island fell by 464 in the first quarter of 1997 from the fourth quarter of 1996.
